column1: # The WRN study's claims in controlled English (docs/method/controlled-english-style-guide.md).
# Each row is a result the hand-built chain states with an opaque predicate
# (docs/06-opaque-predicates-to-propositions.md), or a sentence one rests on: a name's
# introduction, a premise, context. Rows are in the paper's order, so a name or an antecedent comes
# before its use. R1: one claim per sentence. R2: the paper's hedges, qualifiers and scope words are
# kept even where the parse drops them. Statistics stay out. TAB-separated:
#   predicate <TAB> sentence <TAB> source <TAB> intended <TAB> outcome <TAB> skeleton
# source:   the locator in data/slices/PMC6580861.txt (the PMC author manuscript)
# intended: the proposition the sentence should mean, in readable form
# outcome:  over the full lexicon, cap-only: the harness outcome, and why no reading is the claim
# skeleton: the sense-erased skeleton of the reading that is the claim, reviewed against its gloss;
